headline: Revenue and margins surge, buyback guidance raised
summary_short: Moody's grew Q2 FY2026 revenue 15% y/y (16% organic constant currency) to $2,185M and diluted EPS 57% y/y to $5.03, as MIS ratings revenue rose 25% on broad-based issuance strength and MA revenue rose 4% (8% organic constant currency) with ARR up 9% to $3.7B.
summary_long: Revenue rose 15% y/y (16% organic constant currency) to $2,185M, with MIS revenue up 25% on broad-based ratings strength (Corporate Finance +27%, Structured Finance +12%, Financial Institutions +16%, PPIF +38%) and MA revenue up 4% (8% organic constant currency, ARR +9% to $3.7B). MCO operating margin expanded to 47.9% (+480bps) as 5% expense growth trailed 15% revenue growth. Net income rose 52% to $878M, aided by a $181M gain on business divestitures; diluted EPS rose 57% to $5.03. Cash fell to $1,467M from $2,384M (year-end) on $2.165B of H1 buybacks and $365M of dividends. Moody's raised full-year share-repurchase guidance to up to $3.0B and narrowed adjusted diluted EPS guidance to $16.50-$17.00; revenue growth guidance (high-single-digit%) was reaffirmed.

drivers.explanation: MIS revenue rose 25% on broad-based strength: Corporate Finance led by investment-grade and leveraged-finance issuance, Structured Finance on ABS/RMBS/covered-bond growth, Financial Institutions on banking-issuer and private-credit activity, and PPIF on data-center and tech-infrastructure issuance. MA revenue rose 4% (8% organic constant currency).
Diluted EPS rose 57%, tracking the 52% net-income increase plus a 3.2% lower diluted share count from ongoing buybacks.
Tracks the diluted-EPS move on a similarly lower basic weighted-average share count (174.1M vs 179.7M a year ago).

Net income rose 52% on 28% higher operating income plus a $181M pre-tax gain on business divestitures (from the MA Regulatory Solutions sale), which lifted non-operating income to +$125M from -$46M a year ago.

Operating expenses grew only 5% (higher incentive compensation and growth-support costs, moderated by recent divestitures and cost discipline) against 15% revenue growth, expanding MCO operating margin 480bps to 47.9%.
A Yahoo-derived figure Moody's doesn't disclose as a line item; the +18.3% y/y increase tracks the 15% revenue growth against only 5.9% cost-of-revenue growth.
A Yahoo-derived figure tracking the 28% operating-income increase described above.
A Yahoo-derived figure adding depreciation and amortization ($126M, +5% y/y) back to EBIT; tracks the operating-profit increase.
Tracks the 28% operating-income increase plus the $181M gain on business divestitures and slightly lower net interest expense ($58M vs $61M a year ago).
Rose only 5.9% y/y versus 15% revenue growth, consistent with the release's disclosed operating-expense discipline and divestiture-related expense relief.

Fell to $1,467M from $2,384M at year-end 2025 as $2,629M of H1 financing outflows (mainly $2,165M of treasury-share buybacks and $365M of dividends) outpaced $1,718M of operating cash flow and $21M of investing inflows.
Not separately explained in the release; six-month cash flow shows net investment sales/maturities ($106M) exceeding purchases ($74M).

Essentially flat y/y (-0.3%); not separately narrated in the release. This shard metric represents total long-term debt including the current portion ($6,375M non-current + $571M current = $6,946M, reconciling to the release's balance sheet).
The $571M current portion of long-term debt was essentially flat q/q (-0.9%); the year-ago balance was $0, so no y/y comparison is meaningful and q/q is used instead.
Fell 23% y/y to $3,025M as roughly $2,165M of H1 treasury-share buybacks and $365M of dividends outpaced $1,539M of H1 net income added to retained earnings; not separately explained in the release.
Diluted share count fell 3.2% y/y to 174.5M, consistent with the disclosed ~$2.2 billion of year-to-date share repurchases.
CEO Rob Fauber called the results "exceptional," citing strong execution and growing demand for "trusted, decision-grade intelligence" as capital markets evolve and AI transforms workflows.

That exhibit URL was fetched directly and used as the primary document and source_url. All KPI actual values and y/y comparatives reconcile exactly against this release's own comparative columns (revenue, operating expenses, operating income, net income, basic/diluted EPS, income before income taxes, and diluted weighted-average shares all matched to the dollar/cent). One reconciliation note: the shard's long_term_debt_usd_m ($6,946M) equals the release's non-current long-term debt ($6,375M) plus its current portion ($571M) -- our shard convention totals gross long-term debt before current-liability reclassification, distinct from the release's balance-sheet split. Short-term debt has no meaningful y/y comparison because the year-ago current-portion balance was $0, so its delta is reported q/q instead. Gross profit, EBIT, and EBITDA are Yahoo-computed figures, not company-disclosed non-GAAP line items -- this release does not report 'gross profit', 'EBIT', or an 'EBITDA' figure at all. On guidance: the release explicitly says 'raised' only for full-year share-repurchase guidance (to up to $3.0 billion) and explicitly 'Reaffirmed' full-year revenue-growth guidance (high-single-digit percent, no exact bounds given) -- both captured with an explicit move. Diluted EPS, Adjusted Diluted EPS (release calls this change 'narrowed', not raised/lowered), Operating Margin, Operating Cash Flow, and Free Cash Flow guidance all changed numerically from the prior disclosure but without the release using raised/lowered/held language, so move is recorded as null for those per the hard rule that moves require explicit statement.
